newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa loses top man recruited from UAP.
newsitem.headline: Axa loses top man recruited from UAP.

text.p: Dominique Bazy, one of the top executives recruited from Union des Assurances de Paris when the French insurer was taken over by rival Axa late last year, has resigned from the new merged group, Axa announced on Monday.
Bazy, who was a member of Axa's executive committee, "chose to leave the Axa group because he wished to have more operational responsibilities," Axa said in a statement.
The French newspaper Le Monde reported that Bazy, who had been chairman of UAP France, would move to German insurer Allianz to take over as chairman of its French unit, replacing Roberto Gavazzi.
Allianz France said it could neither "confirm nor deny" the newspaper report. Axa said Bazy was on vacation and also could not confirm the report.
Insurance analysts saw the announcement of Bazy's departure as further confirmation Axa would be the dominant force in the new merged company which is the world's second largest insurance group.
"It's clear that Axa people will be in the driver's seat," said one analyst.
Bazy, who had been the third highest executive at UAP, had been regarded as one of UAP's most able senior executives.
Bazy was principal shareholder representative for insurance operations in all countries except France, the United States and life operations in Britain.

Bazy had indicated to Axa chairman Claude Bebear and UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann at the time of the merger that he wanted a more hands-on position in the new merged group "but it was not possible", an Axa spokeswoman said.
Axa said a replacement for Bazy, who had forged a double reputation for himself as a banker and an insurer, would be appointed within the next two weeks.
Axa insisted when the deal was announced that it represented a "friendly operation between equals."
But the executive lineup of the new merged group was dominated by Axa appointments.
